entry.title: Daytripping to Rye
entry.content:
It’s been a while since we went on a proper day trip, so after a bit of googling, we decided to head to Rye.

This medieval town is just an hour from London and turned out to be well worth a visit. Very picturesque and not too crowded, with lots of cute old houses lining small, cobbled streets. It’s fascinating, too, that it used to be a seaside town, but the sea is now 2 miles away!

I particularly enjoyed the view from the tower of the 900-year-old church, a beer in the garden of the Ypres Castle Inn and a nice lunch at The Union Rye.

A very nice day out!

entry.title: End-of-summer recap
entry.content:
Here’s what’s been going on since my “summer so far” recap at the end of July:

  • On an overall level, life has felt a bit in limbo while we’re waiting to complete the purchase and move into our new flat. Living in a temporary place makes everything feel like one big procrastination! 😤
  • I kept spending time playing around with my blog and vibe-coded several new features: a photo archive, dark mode, comments on posts (but you’ll have to email me your comments, and I post them 😅), site search, a publishing calendar on the archive page and a custom 404 page.
  • I did do a trip, to Sweden, working remotely for a week and taking another week off. I enjoyed nature and my little boat, before it was time to go back.
  • Speaking of travel, I spent hours creating a map of the places I’ve been to.
  • It was good fun going to see the recording of Live at the Apollo.
  • I switched to using Kagi as my search engine, paying a subscription fee to get real search results instead of ads.
  • The best meal I had was at Poon’s in Somerset House.
  • I did a bit of shopping, getting myself an iPad again, a new bag for my EDC and some dungarees. I also bought not one but two pairs of JNCO jeans, which I consider the start of a little collection, with pairs three and four already planned.
  • I rebooted my wardrobe, with the goal of moving from my almost all-black outfits to something more relaxed. It was a fairly thorough process, creating a plan and then a final list, before shopping to plug the gaps and finally doing the switch-over.
  • I also posted about my minimal-ish iPhone setup, my wish list, my little projects, and how I budget.

And now I’m really excited that autumn has arrived. It’s always been my favourite season! 🍂

entry.content:
Yesterday, we ended up leaving home too late to be in the mood for our usual Saturday brunch routine. Instead, we decided to do lunch at Poon’s, a Hong Kong restaurant in Somerset House.

We chose the 3-course set menu, which changes daily, and were served chicken soup, char siu pork, mushroom salad, and vegetables. It was all very nice, and the quality felt very high. It was also nice to sit at the counter and watch the chefs at work.

We will definitely come back for more.

I installed iOS 27 yesterday. Is it just me, or is it the least exciting iOS release ever? 😔

  • You can make UI elements less transparent after they made them transparent last year.
  • You can make the clock on the lock screen smaller after they made it bigger last year.
  • Genmoji is a bit more reliable, but buggier in other ways.
  • You can AI-manipulate photos in ways that make them no longer representative of the photo you took.

Plus, Siri is allegedly less rubbish, but it’s been bad for so long it’s hard to care.

That’s it? 🤨

End of rant.

entry.title: I have an iPad again
entry.content:
Yay, I have an iPad again! 😊

For years, I didn’t have a laptop and used an iPad for everything. These days, they are definitely capable enough, and I strongly disagree with those who say tablets are only for consuming, not creating.

What eventually made me replace the iPad with a laptop, though, was something rather counterintuitive: I wanted something easier to carry around. With the iPad, once you add a keyboard, a stand and a trackpad, you have a great setup for tasks like hobby coding, but it ends up being a lot to carry in your backpack for a session in a cafe.

So, a couple of years ago, I replaced it with a MacBook Air.

I love the MacBook, but there have still been situations where I have missed the iPad. Reading the newspaper or a book on a laptop just doesn’t feel right. And undeniably, a laptop is much less convenient when you want to watch an episode of a K-drama on the plane. And using a laptop in bed just isn’t very ergonomic or relaxing at all. And lastly, and ironically: the portability. For the times when I don’t need a keyboard and trackpad, it feels silly wearing a backpack just to carry a backpack just to fit the laptop

So, I’ve been thinking lately: why not both?

I waited for Apple’s launch event on Wednesday, just to make sure they didn’t release anything interesting right after I bought the iPad.

With this being a secondary device, I settled for the iPad A16, a.k.a. the standard iPad. I’m very happy with it so far. It’s definitely quick enough, the screen is perfectly fine, and unless Apple get their act together, the lack of Apple AI is almost a good thing.

entry.title: Thoughts on Apple’s latest launch event
entry.content:
Some thoughts from watching Apple’s “Surprise and Shine” event yesterday:

  • With all the leaks beforehand, the surprise element the name promised was non-existent. I very much miss when there was at least something you weren’t expecting.
  • Calling it an “event” is just taking the piss. Ever since they started pre-recording the whole thing during Covid, it’s really just a 75-minute-long commercial.
  • I literally fell asleep during the iPhone 18 Pro presentation. CPU cores, blah blah, GPU, blah blah, Neural Engine, blah blah 💤 The camera seems nice, though.
  • The iPhone Duo with its unfoldable screen seems technically very impressive. However, making it wider than the Pro Max, where I already can’t reach things with my thumb, seems like a wrong move. All in all, the whole concept feels like a compromise when it comes to the device you use all the time, just to be able to unfold a bigger screen you might use once in a while. It will no doubt get many fans, but it’s not for me.

I’ve been an Apple fanboy for more than 20 years, and still am. I’m not going anywhere, but we’re definitely on a plateau at the moment. Technical specs keep getting more and more impressive, but there’s nothing genuinely new or exciting.

It feels as if it’s time for them to think different™ again.

entry.title: Thinking about buying a camera
entry.content:
It seems the idea of getting a camera is still stuck in my mind.

I obviously know that my photos are limited more by a lack of skill than by the camera, but I feel strongly that the iPhone relies too much on processing. Take a picture of the mist, and the phone boosts the colours to make it look like a clear day.

There is also something satisfying about using an actual camera. Holding it up to your eye, using a proper viewfinder, to take a picture makes it a more conscious action, different from, let’s say, scrolling Pinterest.

That said, when I say camera, I still mean a compact one, not an SLR. The best camera is the one you have with you, as they say.

When I couldn’t sleep last night, I did some further research. The result is that I’ve moved on from the idea of the Ricoh IV. I don’t think a fixed focal length, and one that requires me to get up close, is for me. Right now, I’m leaning toward the Panasonic Lumix L10 instead.

The important thing now is to make sure my desire for a camera is a real thing and will last, so I don’t end up with an expensive paperweight.

For that reason, I’ll wait until October at least before I take any action.
